sum: A short trek from Dhunche up a forested ridge to the sacred Gosaikunda lakes at 4,380 m. It gains 2,400 m in three days, so pacing matters far more than distance.

guide.note: The Nepal Tourism Board has required foreign trekkers to hire a licensed guide since April 2023, though checks on the trail are inconsistent. On this route a guide's main job is to hold your pace down, spot altitude illness early and organize a descent in the dark if it comes to that. In winter they also judge whether the icy traverse above Laurebina is safe to cross.

access: Buses and jeeps run from Machhapokhari in Kathmandu to Dhunche on the Pasang Lhamu Highway, through Trishuli Bazaar. The Bhote Koshi flood of August 2026 damaged this road around Betrawati; it was reported open again to jeeps and light vehicles that autumn, and the trekking agencies' association listed Gosaikunda as accessible from 22 October 2026. Check whether buses have resumed.

photo.a: The dark blue Gosaikunda lake fills a rocky basin between steep brown slopes, with a path along its left shore and clouds building beyond the outlet.

includes: porter with some agencies only (often about USD 20 a day extra)
Langtang National Park permit and TIMS card
lodge beds and three meals a day on the trek

permits.name: Langtang National Park entry permit
permits.where: At the park checkpoint in Dhunche on the drive to Syabrubesi, or in advance at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu.

permits.name: Trekkers' Information Management System card
permits.where: Only through a registered trekking agency, which applies in the Nepal Tourism Board's online system with your route and your guide's details. Individual trekkers can no longer buy one over the counter.

transportText: Bus or a jeep seat between Kathmandu and Dhunche, each way
tips: If you slept badly or have a headache at Chandanbari, spend a second night there before going higher. The lake will still be there.
Bring enough rupees from Kathmandu for the whole trek; there is no ATM on the trail.
Water is scarce on the ridge above Chandanbari. Fill your bottles at each lodge stop and treat it.
Nights at the lake drop well below freezing even in October. Bring a proper sleeping bag rather than relying on lodge blankets.
Start the descent day early. Tired legs on wet stone steps cause most of the falls.

days.note: The Pasang Lhamu Highway through Trishuli Bazaar, slow and rough in places and on temporary repairs since the August 2026 flood. Park permits are checked as you enter Dhunche. A night at 1,960 m is a useful first step up from Kathmandu.

Cross the Trishuli Khola below town, then climb without a break through oak and rhododendron forest, past the teahouses at Deurali and Dimsa. You finish 1,370 m above Dhunche, far more than the usual daily guideline, so walk slowly, drink often and expect to feel the height in the evening.
why: A climb of 1,370 m in one day, to sleep at 3,330 m. Go slowly, drink plenty, and say so if you get a headache.

days.note: A short day on purpose. The trail leaves the forest at Cholangpati and climbs open hillside to the lodges at Laurebina. Many itineraries go straight on to the lake; stopping here roughly halves the day's gain and is the best protection against altitude illness on this route.
why: Sleeping altitude rises 580 m, over the 500 m guideline, with no rest night before or after.

days.note: Climb to the chorten on the ridge, then follow a narrow path cut across a steep slope, with Saraswati Kunda and Bhairav Kunda below you, to the lodges above the main lake. Walk round the lake in the afternoon. In winter this traverse holds ice and is the most dangerous part of the trek.
why: About 1,400 m gained above 3,000 m without a rest night.

days.note: All the height comes off in one day: 2,400 m of descent on stone steps and forest path. Knees and toes take the punishment, so use poles and stop for a proper lunch at Chandanbari. Sleeping there and finishing next morning is a reasonable alternative.
The same road back through Trishuli Bazaar. Delays for landslides and roadworks are routine, so keep the evening free.
